name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: To improve our self-improvement process, I propose we prioritize reviewing and refining our prompt templates first. This is because well-crafted prompts are crucial for effective engine interactions and routing, and by getting them right, we can significantly enhance our overall performance. By focusing on prompts first, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially delaying work on our routing and code optimizations, but I believe this foundation-laying step is essential for making subsequent improvements more effective. This decision will allow us to build upon a solid base and ultimately achieve our goal of self-improvement more efficiently.

name: Gauge
text: I'm not convinced that refining prompt templates should be our top priority, as it may not address the underlying issues with our engine interactions and routing. A more significant risk is that our engines themselves may be outdated or inefficient, and tweaking prompts won't be enough to overcome these limitations. To settle this, I'd like to see a comparison of the potential gains from prompt refinement versus engine upgrades, to determine which approach would truly have the greatest impact on our performance.
